claim.why_it_matters: The rest of the left column is flattened to one indent level, losing the entry/sub-entry hierarchy.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page 871 (printed folio 849, index letter L) shows a two-level index in the left column: main entries at the margin (for example 'Last-used state 386', 'LC_ALL 64', 'LEADING phrase', 'LINE (LINES) keyword') with sub-entries indented under them ('START statement 531', 'SET statement, locale 517', 'INSPECT statement 462', 'SEND statement 673'). In the markdown, every left-column line from 'START statement 531' to 'SEND statement 673' has the same 3-space indent and ends in a backslash line break, so main entries and sub-entries look alike. A reader can no longer tell that 'SET statement, locale 517' belongs under LC_ALL, or that 'Constant entry 245' and 'START statement 531' belong under 'LENGTH phrase'. The right column keeps the hierarchy with  , which shows the left column lost it. The quotes in the claim match both sources. The only problem is the kind label: nothing is misplaced. The entry/sub-entry nesting has been flattened. The damage is structural and confined to the informative index, so the severity is correct.
verdict.corrected_description: Hierarchy flattened, not misplaced. In the left column of index page 871, from 'START statement 531' through 'SEND statement 673', main entries and sub-entries carry the same 3-space indent, so the parent/child nesting the PDF prints is lost (for example 'LC_ALL 64' / 'SET statement, locale 517'). The text and page numbers are all there. The informative index is the only part affected.
